name: 215 East Twentieth Street — red brick rowhouse with round-headed lights behind its front yard, K01 frontage assembly

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The house claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-2982 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped); the 2009 photographs show it standing. No building or loss date is read for it here (T-3782).

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body at its east wall: row 350.5 and column 399.5 of sheet 35 at full size (T-3782), the line 215 shares with 217's west wall, carried through the T-1250 fit of the sheet (0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom, plus about a pixel, 0.19 m, of reading) and set on 217's own corner so the party wall is one line. Rotation -90.599 degrees, 217's, turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's rear-to-street line, north to East Twentieth Street; v runs west from the east wall, so K01's `south` wall is the party wall with 217 and its `north` wall the party wall with 213.
placement.symbolic_location: 215 E. Twentieth Street, parcel e20th_215 (data/street_grid/1904.json), south side of East Twentieth Street, the district's named context buildings off Prairie Avenue: East Twentieth Street between Indiana and Prairie, and Calumet Avenue between 20th and 21st Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: The main body: 11.43 m from the rear wall (row 350.5, in line with 217's) to the front (row 289, a solid line under the sheet's dashed one at row 287), and 7.15 m along the front from the party wall with 217 (column 399.5) to the party wall with 213 (column 361), read off sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size (T-3782) at 0.1858 m a pixel. The front stands 17.5 px (3.25 m) behind 213's and 217's, which are on the street line (row 271.5): the sheet's front yard. The draft's fit had read an 11.0 by 5.75 m body; the corner moves 0.67 m east and 0.4 m south.

stories.note: '3' printed at the body's north-west corner on the 1911 sheet: three storeys.

construction.note: The sheet colours the body brick; photograph 224 shows a red pressed-brick front with stone sills, lintels and arch heads.

principal_floor_m.note: The principal floor about 0.9 m over the yard: in photograph 224 the door's sill stands two or three risers over the yard's walk and the round-headed lights' sills about half a metre over the door's; its exact height unread (T-3783 solves the camera).

storey_heights_m.note: In photograph 224 the ground storey, from the door's sill to the light stone course under the second storey's sills, is about 3.4 m at the front's own scale (its 7.15 m width across the frame); the second and third storeys are cut off by the frame and take the street's usual 3.4 and 3.0 m. T-3783 holds them to the pictures.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A brick front's usual thickness on the street; unread.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A party or flank wall's usual 13 in.; unread.

service_wall_brick.note: The rear's common brick, as the street's other K01 houses; unread.

eave_overhang_m.note: The bracketed cornice's projection over the front, the kit's; the photographs do not reach the wall head.

face_brick.note: Photograph 224: the street front is red pressed brick in a fine joint; the two flanks are party walls with 213 and 217 and unseen, laid in common buff.

street_front_round_heads.note: Photograph 224: the ground storey's two lights and its door are round-headed under plain stone arch heads, their imposts level; the second storey's lights are square-headed. The kit's shallow key at each crown is not read (the print is too small to show one).

street_front_trim.note: Photograph 224: the second storey's lights stand on stone sills under flat stone lintels; the ground storey's round heads take the arch heads above, the third storey (out of frame) the same lintel as the second.

wall_head.note: The register's 'flat behind a cornice' row; no photograph reaches the wall head, so the kit's bracketed cornice.

roof_form.note: Flat behind the cornice, the register's row and the rowhouses' usual; the roof is unseen.

roof_pitch_deg.note: A flat deck's fall to the rear; unread.

roof_covering.note: A painted flat-seam tin deck, as the street's other flat roofs; unread.

stoop_width_m.note: The kit's stoop under the arched door; its steps hidden by the yard's planting in photograph 224.

entrance_bay.note: Photograph 224: the door is the front's west bay, beside the party wall with 213 (K01's `north`).

front_bays.note: The street front, counted from the east corner (the party wall with 217): the two round-headed lights and the door, read across photograph 224 at the front's own 7.15 m (about 76 px a metre at the print's double size): the lights' axes 1.15 and 3.6 m in, the door's 6.0 m (its 1.4 m opening clear of the west corner).

side_bays.note: The east flank is a party wall with 217 for its whole depth (sheet 35): no lights.

north_bays.note: The west flank is a party wall with 213 for its whole depth (sheet 35): no lights.

rear_bays.note: Two lights in the rear wall: unseen.

sash_by_storey.note: Photograph 224: the ground storey's round-headed lights about 0.95 m wide and 2.3 m to the crown of the arch, their sills about half a metre over the door's; the second storey's square-headed lights as wide, their sills on the stone course just over the floor. The third storey is out of frame and takes a shorter light.

basement_lights.note: A low area light under each ground-storey light, the kit's: the yard's planting hides the plinth in photograph 224.

window_kit.note: The kit's sash; the 2009 glazing is not read as 1904's.

entrance_kit.note: Photograph 224: the door stands in a deep round-arched opening in the front's west bay, about 1.4 m wide and 2.9 m to the crown, its leaves set back in the reveal, a few steps over the yard; the kit's deep-arched double door. The front yard is the 4.75 m between the front and the walk's inner edge (the sheet's 3.25 m setback behind 217's line, and 217's 1.55 m strip).

chimneys.note: One stack on the party wall with 213: no picture shows the stacks.

boundary.note: A low iron railing on a stone curb along the walk's inner edge, 4.7 m before the front, with a walk gate: photograph 224 shows the yard closed by a tall iron fence and gate in 2009, a later one; the kit's spear railing, its 1904 pattern unread. The lot lines are the parcel's (sheet 35 columns 360.7 and 399.2), its east one taken on the party wall, a few centimetres off, inside a pixel.

yard.note: A walk of stone flags from the gate to the stoop's foot across the front yard; the yard's 2009 planting is not read as 1904's.

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3 brick dwelling (D) set back behind a front yard closed by a dashed line, a shorter body than its neighbours'. Carried to 1904 on the T-2982 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Jyoti Srivastava, 'Three Row Houses at East Cullerton', Chicago - Architecture & Cityscape (blog), September 2009: colour photographs of 213, 215 and 217 E. Cullerton Street (East Twentieth Street before the 1930s renaming), c. 2009.
what_it_supplies: 217's street front: two round-headed lights under the oriel and the door in a carved stone surround west of them (223)
217's corner oriel: a rounded bay sheathed in copper over the ground storey, two storeys tall, its lights bent round it, on a rounded copper underside (106, 220, 223)
217's walls: red brick over a red sandstone base course, stone sills and heads, the ground storey's round-headed openings (106, 220, 223)
a steep gable with a finial over 217's east flank (106)

215's street front: red pressed brick, the ground storey's two round-headed lights and round-arched door in its west bay under plain stone heads, the second storey's square-headed lights on stone sills under flat stone lintels, set back behind a front yard (224)

213's street front: red, four storeys, the third storey's lights round-headed, a deep bracketed cornice returning along the east flank (225); the ground storey's door with a transom between two framed lights under a broad pedimented hood on consoles (222)
213's east flank: buff common brick where it stands before and over 215, with lights near the front (220, 225)
what_it_does_not_supply: a 1904 date: the photographs are of the surviving house in 2009
the rear, 217's west flank, 213's west flank and the roofs behind the gable and the cornices
dimensions: no scale stands in the frame

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 35.
what_it_supplies: Footprints, lots and street widths from 20th to 22nd Street between Indiana and Calumet, as of 1911, at the copy's coarser resolution
The position of Twentieth Street, which is vacated between Indiana and Calumet today
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
Any lake edge: the sheet ends at Calumet Avenue

research_note: T-3782 (piece 2 of T-1939, the X01 package of the T-1837 programme) refines the district draft (T-2982) in place under the same id: the house is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — a K03 red pressed-brick front with stone sills and flat stone lintels, the ground storey's two round-headed lights and round-arched door, three storeys under a K10 bracketed cornice and a flat deck, set back behind its front yard — instead of the draft builder. What is read: sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size (the outline set back behind a dashed line, '3') and photograph 224 of the surviving house (2009, forms only). What is not built, and why, is the liberty L-k01-213-215-e20th-3782; T-3783 solves the photographs' cameras and works the match down.
